edges.detail: CTEPH follows acute PE in about 0.6% of all comers and 3.2% of survivors (meta-analysis of 16 studies).
CTEPH is a relatively common, serious complication of PE.
CTEPH is a rare complication of acute PE, symptomatic or not (ERS statement).
In Japan, 2.3% of acute PE patients were diagnosed with CTEPH within 3 years (DOAC era).
Previous VTE (OR 4.5) and recurrent VTE (OR 14.5) are associated with CTEPH.
Recurrent VTE (OR 3.2) and unprovoked PE (OR 4.1) raise the risk of CTEPH after PE.
CTEPH follows DVT less often than PE: 0.3% and 1.3% at 2 and 10 years after DVT.
CTEPH develops most commonly after PE and less frequently after DVT.
Japanese women with CTEPH had less DVT and fewer acute embolic episodes than men.
More than half of CTEPH patients, especially Japanese, have no prior DVT or coagulation abnormality.
CTEPD is the broader term; CTEPH refers to the patients with pulmonary hypertension.
CTEPH and CTEPD describe chronic thromboembolic occlusions with or without PH at rest.
Lupus anticoagulant / antiphospholipid antibodies are associated with CTEPH (OR 4.2).
About 12% of CTEPH patients carry antiphospholipid antibodies (meta-analysis).
Phospholipid-dependent antibodies were found in 20% of CTEPH patients.
In one UK study antiphospholipid antibodies were not increased in CTEPH.
CTEPH was found in 3.8% of an APS cohort.
8.6% of CTEPH patients had a splenectomy, against 2.5% in IPAH.
Splenectomy (OR 13), VA shunts (OR 13) and chronic inflammatory disorders raise the risk of CTEPH after PE.
The 5-year cumulative incidence of CTEPH after splenectomy was 3.2%.
Against PE controls, only a trend towards more splenectomy and non-O blood group remained.
VA shunts and infected pacemakers are strongly associated with CTEPH (OR 76).
VA-shunt carriers with shunt infection are at increased risk of CTEPH; staphylococcal DNA was found in their thrombi.
Thyroid replacement therapy (OR 6.1) and malignancy (OR 3.8) emerged as CTEPH risk factors.
A quarter of operable CTEPH patients had thyroid disease, mostly hypothyroidism.
Review: splenectomy, cancer, VA shunt, chronic inflammation, antiphospholipid antibodies and hypothyroidism raise CTEPH risk.
A history of malignancy (OR 3.8) emerged as a CTEPH risk factor.
Against PE controls, malignancy and other conditions did not raise the risk of CTEPH.
10.6% of 1,270 Japanese CTEPH patients had a history of cancer.
Cancer is a known risk factor for CTEPH.
Chronic inflammatory disorders such as IBD and osteomyelitis were associated with CTEPH (OR 67, wide CI).
IBD was among the risk factors identified in a CTEPH series.
Against PE controls, the conditions studied (including IBD) were equally frequent.
Osteomyelitis was among the chronic inflammatory disorders associated with CTEPH.
Splenectomy, VA shunt, central lines, IBD and osteomyelitis were associated with CTEPH development.
Half of the PH patients with an MPN had CTEPH; PV and ET were mostly related to CTEPH.
Three of 40 CTEPH patients carried JAK2 p.Val617Phe, each with an MPN; more than expected.
5.4% of CTEPH patients in a Japanese registry had an MPN.
PV and ET were generally related to CTEPH among MPN patients with PH.
PV and ET were generally related to CTEPH among MPN patients with PH.
9.4% of CTEPH patients carried a CHIP mutation (VAF >= 2%).
20.1% of Japanese CTEPH patients had variants in clonal-haematopoiesis genes.
Thrombotic lesions are a major component of PH in sickle cell disease.
A third of haemolytic-anaemia PH patients had CTEPH (50% of SCD).
Haemoglobinopathies and congenital haemolytic anaemia predispose to CTEPH.
Hereditary thrombotic risk factors were not increased in CTEPH.
Factor V Leiden was more frequent in white CTEPH patients (29% vs 7.8%).
About one in seven CTEPH patients has a congenital thrombophilia, mostly protein S or C deficiency.
Prothrombin rs1799963 was more common in CTEPH than in controls.
In Chinese CTEPH patients, 9.8% had congenital thrombophilia (protein C/S, antithrombin); no FVL or F2 G20210A.
Non-O blood groups are associated with CTEPH (OR 2.1).
The association of CTEPH with prior VTE and non-O blood groups was confirmed.
The CTEPH GWAS found loci at ABO, FGG, F11, MYH7B and HLA-DRA.
Elevated FVIII was more prevalent in CTEPH (41%) than in controls (5%).
FVIII and VWF were higher in CTEPH than in other PH.
Review: antiphospholipid antibodies, increased FVIII, non-O blood groups and chronic inflammation are the most consistent risk factors.
CTEPH patients had decreased ADAMTS13 and increased VWF.
VWF is increased in plasma and pulmonary endothelium of CTEPH patients.
CTEPH patients with rare STAB2 variants had higher VWF and FVIII.
ADAMTS13 stayed low after endarterectomy and was equally reduced in CTED.
Dysfibrinogenaemia was found in 5 of 33 CTEPH patients.
The fibrinogen Aalpha Thr312Ala allele increased the risk of CTEPH.
Thr312Ala was a risk factor for CTEPH but not PE in Chinese patients.
FGA rs6050 is associated with VTE and CTEPH (meta-analysis).
The CTEPH GWAS found a locus at F11.
F11 rs2289252 was more frequent in CTEPH (OR 1.55).
D-dimer and CRP at diagnosis predict outcome in CTEPH.
D-dimer is insensitive and nonspecific for diagnosing CTEPH.
A lower D-dimer at the index PE predicted later CTEPH in a Japanese registry.
CTEPH patients had a lower platelet count, higher MPV and more spontaneous aggregation.
Review: high platelet counts are among the plasmatic factors proposed to cause vessel obliteration.
Platelets of Japanese CTEPH patients are highly activated and hyperresponsive to thrombin.
Lp(a) was higher in CTEPH than in PPH and controls (one small study).
PAH is group 1 and CTEPH group 4 of the PH classification (2022 ESC/ERS guidelines).
Non-operable CTEPH resembles IPAH more than operable CTEPH in its risk factors.
The CTEPH GWAS found no association shared with IPAH.
